fullPassage:
How do we open ourselves up to new possibilities? One of the ways to do this is to connect things that look separate. This can be incredibly pleasing as it helps us to see the world in a different light and gain a greater appreciation for the interrelation of all things. Here are three artists who are willing to experiment with this approach.

Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller living in Milan, Italy, who has been delighting his viewers with his unique artworks on social media. He draws illustrations on top of photos of landmarks or buildings and offers whole new ways to see them. To breathe life into well-known structures around the world, he often uses iconic pop culture characters.

His unique twists sometimes turn what we consider dull and boring into something delightful. To him, a bridge is a net, and a road is a bowling lane. After finding whatever is common in two unrelated things, he connects them smoothly in his digital drawing.

His work combines his passion for traveling and drawing. Exploring new places and learning about new cultures inspire his artistic mind to come up with new ideas for his art. Many of his digital illustrations transform the most historic buildings of the world into new objects that you would like to see again. For example, he added images of ice cream cones onto the scenic photo of St. Basil's Cathedral in Moscow, the capital of Russia. The Leaning Tower of Pisa, one of the most remarkable architectural structures in Italy, appeared to be a camera lens to him.

Paintings of Rob Gonsalves, a Canadian magic realist artist, combine two different points of view. They give the viewer the visual illusion that they are looking at two unrelated realities flawlessly fused in one painting. They usually depict landscapes and objects that seem to change from one thing to another.

When you look at the top right corner of the painting above, you can see a kid jumping on his bed. However, as you move your eyes across, the bedcovers change into fields, which a girl now appears to be flying over. This is how the visual illusion is created: an object is gradually changed through a series of similar shapes into something entirely different in a single scene. At the same time, two different parts of the same scene are constructed at different scales. The result is an unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.

This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your perception. It makes you question what is real. Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear boundary between the multiple stories they tell, which forces the viewer to jump back and forth between them. Tracing the transitions, you get that delightful Ah-ha! feeling as you try to decide exactly where one world transforms into another.

When we look at shadows of objects in real life, most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them into art forms. He lets his creativity flow to make beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.

His playful shadow art illustrations are made by adding his own doodles to shadows cast from everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. In one image, the shadow from a key is reinterpreted as a DJ wearing headphones. In another, a potato peeler creates the perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In his art, the shadow from a glass becomes a pool.

He uses a very simple process to draw his pictures. To start the process, all he needs to do is prepare a plain object, a piece of paper, and a light. Then he puts the object on the paper and turns on the light. He just starts moving the light around and places the object in different positions. He keeps a very open mind and tries not to have an idea in advance about what the result should be.

If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take another object, and then I just start playing around with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I can create whatever I want, he says. His free artistic interpretation of shadows means that the possibilities for creating new doodles are endless.

In fact, it was by accident that he started making his art pieces. While he was working on a new script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of a cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. He completed the image with a few lines, took a picture and shared it on the Internet. The reactions were so positive that he challenged himself to make one shadow image every day.

Art can inspire you to see the world from a new angle. Connecting ideas that at first glance appear unrelated is a powerful tool for exploring the beauty of the world around us. To make such connections, all you need is your imaginative power.

questions.passage: How do we open ourselves up to new possibilities? One of the ways to do this is to connect things that look (A)[separate / identical]. This can be incredibly pleasing as it helps us to see the world in a different light and gain a greater (B)[appreciation / rejection] for the interrelation of all things. Here are three artists who are willing to (C)[experiment / interfere] with this approach. Meet Robin Yayla, a visual storyteller living in Milan, Italy, who has been delighting his viewers with his unique artworks on social media. He draws illustrations on top of photos of landmarks or buildings and offers whole new ways to see them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 분리되어 보이는 것들을 연결하는 것이 방법 중 하나다. 이것은 모든 것의 상호관계에 대해 더 큰 감사(appreciation)를 얻도록 돕는다. 이러한 접근법으로 실험(experiment)하려는 세 예술가를 소개한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① separate — appreciation — experiment
❌ ② identical — appreciation — experiment
❌ ③ separate — rejection — interfere
❌ ④ identical — rejection — interfere
✅ (A) separate: '분리된' 것들을 connect하는 맥락. identical(동일한)은 연결할 필요가 없으므로 부적절. ✅ (B) appreciation: '감사, 이해'. rejection(거부)은 긍정적 맥락과 반대. ✅ (C) experiment: 'experiment with'는 '~을 실험하다'. interfere(방해하다)는 부적절.
det.tip: separate(분리된) ↔ identical(동일한). appreciation(감사) ↔ rejection(거부). experiment with = ~을 시도하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Robin Yayla는 독특한 작품으로 시청자들을 기쁘게 하고(delighting) 있다. 잘 알려진 건물에 생명을 불어넣기(breathe life into) 위해 상징적인(iconic) 대중문화 캐릭터를 사용한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① disappointing — breathe — iconic
✅ ② delighting — breathe — iconic
❌ ③ delighting — drain — obscure
❌ ④ disappointing — drain — obscure

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그의 독특한 변형은 지루한 것을 즐거운(delightful) 것으로 바꾼다. 관련 없는(unrelated) 두 가지의 공통점을 찾아 매끄럽게(smoothly) 연결한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① tedious — unrelated — smoothly
❌ ② delightful — connected — roughly
✅ ③ delightful — unrelated — smoothly
❌ ④ tedious — connected — roughly
✅ (A) delightful: dull and boring의 반대인 '즐거운'. tedious(지루한)는 dull과 같은 의미라 변화가 없음. ✅ (B) unrelated: '관련 없는' 것들의 공통점을 찾는 맥락. connected(연결된)이면 공통점을 찾을 필요 없음. ✅ (C) smoothly: '매끄럽게' 연결. roughly(거칠게)는 예술적 연결과 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: delightful(즐거운) ↔ tedious(지루한). unrelated(무관한) ↔ connected(연결된). smoothly(매끄럽게) ↔ roughly(거칠게).

det.analysis: ✅ ④ illusion: 원문 그대로. 시각적 착시. ✅ ② flawlessly: 원문 그대로. 완벽하게. ✅ ③ depict: 원문 그대로. 묘사하다. ❌ ① partially → entirely: 원문은 '완전히 다른' 것으로 변한다. partially(부분적으로)는 반의어.
det.tip: entirely(완전히) ↔ partially(부분적으로). 착시의 핵심은 완전히 다른 것으로의 변환.

questions.passage: This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your ①<u>perception</u>. Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear ②<u>boundary</u> between the multiple stories they tell. Tracing the ③<u>transitions</u>, you get that delightful Ah-ha! feeling as you try to decide exactly where one world ④<u>preserves</u> into another.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 이런 착시는 당신의 ①인식(perception)을 비트는 재미있는 방식이다. 불분명한 ②경계(boundary)가 있다. ③전환(transitions)을 추적하면서 한 세계가 다른 세계로 ④보존된다(preserves).
det.analysis: ✅ ① perception: 원문 그대로. 인식. ✅ ② boundary: 원문 그대로. 경계. ✅ ③ transitions: 원문 그대로. 전환. ❌ ④ preserves → transforms: 원문은 한 세계가 다른 세계로 '변형된다'. preserves(보존하다)는 변형과 반대 의미.
det.tip: transforms(변형하다) ↔ preserves(보존하다). 착시 예술에서 핵심은 하나가 다른 것으로 transform되는 것.

✅ ③ advance
❌ ② detail
❌ ① return
❌ ④ contrast

det.tip: in advance = 미리, 사전에. advance(진전) → in advance(미리). 'have an idea in advance' = '미리 생각을 가지다'.

At the same time, two different parts of the same scene are constructed at different <u>scales</u>. The result is an unexpected and seemingly impossible whole.

This kind of illusion has a fun way of twisting your perception. It makes you question what is real. Most of his incredible paintings have an unclear boundary between the multiple stories they tell, which forces the viewer to jump back and forth between them. Tracing the transitions, you get that delightful Ah-ha! feeling as you try to decide exactly where one world transforms into another.

When we look at shadows of objects in real life, most of us think nothing of them. Belgian artist and film-maker Vincent Bal, however, turns them into art forms. He lets his creativity flow to make beautiful and meaningful scenes with shadows.

His playful shadow art illustrations are made by adding his own doodles to shadows cast from everyday objects, like a flower or a glass. In one image, the shadow from a key is reinterpreted as a DJ wearing headphones. In another, a potato peeler creates the perfectly shaped frame for a piano. In his art, the shadow from a glass becomes a pool.

He uses a very simple process to draw his pictures. To start the process, all he needs to do is prepare a plain object, a piece of paper, and a light. Then he puts the object on the paper and turns on the light. He just starts moving the light around and places the object in different positions. He keeps a very open mind and tries not to have an idea in advance about what the result should be.

If I try to shape a shadow into a certain form, it always feels a bit forced. If nothing comes, I take another object, and then I just start playing around with it until suddenly I see something. In this way, I can create whatever I want, he says. His free artistic interpretation of shadows means that the possibilities for creating new doodles are endless.

In fact, it was by accident that he started making his art pieces. While he was working on a new script, he suddenly noticed how the shadow of a cup on his desk looked like a little elephant. Art can inspire you to see the world from a new angle. Connecting ideas that at first glance appear unrelated is a powerful tool for exploring the beauty of the world around us. To make such connections, all you need is your imaginative power.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 scales의 이 글에서의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 같은 장면의 서로 다른 부분이 다른 크기(scales)로 구성된다. 그 결과 예상치 못한 전체가 된다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 저울, 체중계
✅ ③ 크기, 규모
❌ ② 비늘, 껍질
❌ ④ 음계, 음역
✅ 크기, 규모: 'at different scales'는 '서로 다른 규모로'. 그림에서 한 장면의 부분들이 다른 크기로 그려지는 것. ❌ 저울: 무게 측정 도구. 회화 맥락 부적절. ❌ 비늘: 생물학 용어. ❌ 음계: 음악 용어.
det.tip: scale의 다의어: (1) 저울 (2) 규모, 크기 (3) 비늘 (4) 음계. 이 글에서는 '규모' 의미.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a false or misleading image presented to the vision; something that deceives by producing a false impression of reality"

det.korean: 시각에 제시되는 잘못된 이미지; 현실에 대한 잘못된 인상을 만들어 속이는 것 → illusion(착시, 환상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① illustration
❌ ② interpretation
✅ ④ illusion
❌ ③ imagination
✅ illusion: '착시, 환상'으로 영영풀이와 정확히 일치. ❌ illustration(삽화): 그림의 한 종류. ❌ interpretation(해석): 의미를 파악하는 것. ❌ imagination(상상력): 마음속으로 그리는 능력.
det.tip: illusion(착시, 환상): il-(안으로) + lus(놀다) → 마음을 속여 노는 것. illustration, interpretation, imagination과 혼동 주의.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 모든 것의 상호관계에 대해 더 큰 감사/이해(appreciation)를 얻다.
det.analysis: appreciate(동사: 감사하다) → appreciation(명사: 감사, 이해). 'a greater __'에서 관사+형용사 뒤이므로 명사가 필요.
det.tip: appreciate(v.) → appreciation(n.). -tion 접미사는 동사를 명사로 변환. 'gain appreciation for' = '~에 대한 이해를 얻다'.

det.korean: 그런 연결을 하려면, 당신에게 필요한 것은 상상력이 풍부한(imaginative) 힘이다.

det.tip: imagine(v.) → imaginative(adj.) → imagination(n.). imaginative power = 상상력. imaginary(상상의, 가상의)와 혼동 주의.

det.korean: 사실 그가 작품을 만들기 시작한 것은 우연히(by accident)였다. 새 대본을 작업하다가 컵의 그림자가 코끼리처럼 보인다는 것을 갑자기 알아챘다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① intention
❌ ② invitation
✅ ④ instruction
❌ ③ accident

det.tip: by accident = 우연히 ↔ on purpose = 의도적으로. accident(사고, 우연).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음 보기에 무관해 보이는 아이디어를 연결하는 것은 우리 주변 세계의 아름다움을 탐구하기 위한 강력한(powerful) 도구이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② powerful
❌ ① harmful
❌ ③ useless
❌ ④ trivial
✅ powerful: '강력한'. 무관한 것을 연결하는 것이 세계의 아름다움을 탐구하는 강력한 도구라는 긍정적 맥락. ❌ harmful(해로운): 긍정적 맥락과 반대. ❌ useless(쓸모없는): 긍정적 맥락과 반대. ❌ trivial(사소한): 긍정적 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: powerful(강력한) tool = 강력한 도구. 예술이 세계를 새롭게 보게 하는 힘에 대한 글의 결론.
